subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should OpenClaw fix this issue by making native OpenAI eligible for existing cache-TTL pruning, or should it wait for a provider-agnostic or retention-aware pruning design?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but changing OpenAI eligibility activates pruning for existing configs and needs an explicit OpenAI cache-retention/session-policy decision before the open fix lands.

options.title: Prove and land the linked OpenAI eligibility fix
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95859 as the fix path, require redacted native OpenAI idle-gap proof, and document or test the intended OpenAI TTL behavior before merge.

options.title: Replace with retention-aware pruning
options.body: Close or supersede the linked PR after opening a narrower design that separates pruning policy from provider cache-TTL eligibility.

options.title: Keep OpenAI ineligible for now
options.body: Leave the issue open as a known limitation until maintainers decide OpenAI cache semantics are safe enough for pruning.

recommendation.title: Prove and land the linked OpenAI eligibility fix
recommendation.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95859 as the fix path, require redacted native OpenAI idle-gap proof, and document or test the intended OpenAI TTL behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc authored the latest release commit that introduced the current cache-TTL helper and adjacent prompt-caching docs, so he is the strongest available policy owner from history.
